problem_statement: In a network running RPL in storing mode with receiver-based TSCH scheduling, a node sends a link-local-addressed unicast (for example an RPL DIO probe, or any traffic addressed to a neighbor's link-local address rather than its global address) to a link-layer-reachable neighbor that is neither its RPL parent nor one of its children — a sibling that has no unicast TSCH cell dedicated to it. Instead of being delivered, the packet is never transmitted: it remains stuck and the queue backing traffic to that neighbor fills up, so no traffic to the neighbor can get through. As a result the destination never receives the packet. Correct behavior is that such a link-local unicast to a reachable sibling, even one with no dedicated unicast cell, is delivered and the destination receives it (in the test, the receiving node must receive all ten packets sent by the sender).
causal_chain: The test scenario places two sibling nodes that join the RPL DODAG as direct children of the root while out of range of each other, then moves one next to the other so the two become link-layer reachable but remain siblings: neither is the other's RPL parent or child, and neither holds a unicast cell dedicated to the other. The sender then sends link-local-addressed UDP packets to the sibling. Under the unfixed behavior, the sender treats this reachable sibling as having a dedicated unicast link even though no such cell exists in its schedule, so the frames are held for a slot that never arrives and accumulate without ever being transmitted; the receiver never reaches the required count and the simulation times out and fails. After the fix, the link-local traffic to this sibling is sent in a way that reaches it, and the receiver receives all ten packets, so the scenario passes.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: In a network that uses receiver-based TSCH scheduling together with RPL operating in storing mode, link-local unicast packets addressed to a neighbor that is neither the node's RPL parent nor one of its children fail to be delivered. This covers traffic such as RPL DIO probes sent to a sibling that shares the same parent, as well as any layer-2 unicast to a link-layer neighbor that does not use a global IP address and is instead reached via the parent. Although that neighbor is physically in range, the scheduler still selects a dedicated unicast slot for it even though no such slot actually exists in the node's TSCH schedule. The consequence is that the frames are never transmitted, accumulate in the node's output queue, and eventually fill that queue, blocking all traffic to that neighbor. The required behavior is that such link-local traffic to a sibling be delivered through the node's normal shared schedule instead of a dedicated link that is not present in the schedule.
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "Although that neighbor is physically in range, the scheduler still selects a dedicated unicast slot for it even though no such slot actually exists in the node's TSCH schedule."; "The required behavior is that such link-local traffic to a sibling be delivered through the node's normal shared schedule instead of a dedicated link that is not present in the schedule.". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally
